summary.title: Einstein vs Maxwell: Is gravitation a curvature of space, a field in flat space, or both?
summary.executive_summary: This paper investigates the foundational interpretation of gravitation, contrasting Einstein's General Relativity (GTR) as a curvature of space with a Maxwell-like field theory in flat Minkowski space. The author derives the gravitational energy-momentum tensor from the Einstein equations using a field-theoretic approach in Minkowski space, demonstrating that for flat space cosmology, the negative gravitational energy exactly cancels the positive material energy, resulting in a total energy of zero. The study extends this framework to the Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG), a bimetric theory that breaks general coordinate invariance by coupling the Riemann and Minkowski metrics. A key contribution is the analytical solution of a singularity-free version of the Schwarzschild black hole. In this RTG model, the metric components inside the horizon decay rapidly but remain positive, preserving the standard role of time and allowing for the possibility of escape, unlike the standard GTR black hole. The paper further applies this framework to cosmology, showing that the model naturally reproduces the ΛCDM model at late times while predicting a form of inflation at early times. The bimetric terms, associated with a positive cosmological constant, act to cancel the vacuum energy, ensuring the zero-point energy vanishes. The author concludes that while the field-theoretic and curved-space views are equivalent in standard GTR, the bimetric extension makes the 'field in flat space' interpretation more natural, as it explicitly separates the background Minkowski metric from the gravitational field. This approach offers a resolution to the black hole singularity problem and provides a consistent cosmological model where the total energy of the universe is zero.

claims.description: Gravitation can be consistently described as a field in flat Minkowski space with a proper energy-momentum tensor.
The Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG) with a positive cosmological constant resolves the black hole singularity.
The total energy of the universe is zero in this framework.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper investigates the foundational interpretation of gravitation, contrasting Einstein's General Relativity (GTR) as a curvature of space with a Maxwell-like field theory in flat Minkowski space. The author derives the gravitational energy-momentum tensor from the Einstein equations using a field-theoretic approach in Minkowski space, demonstrating that for flat space cosmology, the negative gravitational energy exactly cancels the positive material energy, resulting in a total energy of zero. The study extends this framework to the Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG), a bimetric theory that breaks general coordinate invariance by coupling the Riemann and Minkowski metrics. A key contribution is the analytical solution of a singularity-free version of the Schwarzschild black hole. In this RTG model, the metric components inside the horizon decay rapidly but remain positive, preserving the standard role of time and allowing for the possibility of escape, unlike the standard GTR black hole. The paper further applies this framework to cosmology, showing that the model naturally reproduces the ΛCDM model at late times while predicting a form of inflation at early times. The bimetric terms, associated with a positive cosmological constant, act to cancel the vacuum energy, ensuring the zero-point energy vanishes. The author concludes that while the field-theoretic and curved-space views are equivalent in standard GTR, the bimetric extension makes the 'field in flat space' interpretation more natural, as it explicitly separates the background Minkowski metric from the gravitational field. This approach offers a resolution to the black hole singularity problem and provides a consistent cosmological model where the total energy of the universe is zero.

Research Context
The paper addresses the fundamental difficulty of defining a proper energy-momentum tensor for gravitation in General Relativity. Previous work by Babak and Grishchuk derived a proper tensor using a field theoretic approach in Minkowski space. The Maxwell view of gravitation as a field in flat space was Einstein's starting point. Nathan Rosen proposed a bimetric theory involving both Minkowski and Riemann metrics. Logunov and coworkers developed the Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG) based on this bimetric approach.

Research Question And Hypothesis
The central question is whether gravitation is best described as space curvature, a field in flat space, or both. The hypothesis is that a field theoretic approach in Minkowski space allows for a straightforward derivation of the gravitational energy-momentum tensor. It is hypothesized that in flat space cosmology, gravitational energy is negative and cancels material energy. The study posits that a bimetric coupling breaks general coordinate invariance. The author predicts that a positive cosmological constant leads to a singularity-free Schwarzschild black hole solution. It is expected that the model covers the ΛCDM cosmology and includes early-time inflation.

Methodological Details
The study uses a field theoretic approach in Minkowski space with metric ηµν = diag(1, −1, −1, −1). The Riemann metric tensor gµν is defined via the gravitational field hµν. The acceleration tensor Aµν is defined using Minkowski covariant derivatives. The gravitational energy-momentum tensor τµν is derived as a bilinear form in first order covariant derivatives. The Einstein equations are rewritten in the Newton shape: acceleration = mass−1 × force. Cosmology is described by the Friedman-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric with k=0. The Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG) action includes a bimetric term ρbi coupling the metrics. A positive cosmological constant Λ is chosen, with ρΛ = ρbi. The harmonic condition Dνhµν = 0 is imposed by energy-momentum conservation. The Schwarzschild black hole is analyzed in harmonic coordinates with a small parameter ¯λ.

Procedures And Architectures
The gravitational action SR is expressed in terms of Minkowski covariant first order derivatives. The Lagrangian LR is close to general field theory approaches. The gauge transformation subgroup allows three extra terms in the Lagrangian. The bimetric term acts like a mass term, breaking general coordinate invariance. The parameter ρbi is set equal to ρΛ, leaving one free parameter. The graviton is assigned an imaginary mass, making it a tachyon. The Einstein equations are coupled to matter via the total energy-momentum tensor. The black hole solution is found parametrically using a running variable ξ. The scale η is fixed by demanding u′(0) = 0 for the central mass. The transition layer width is compared to the Planck length.

Key Results
For flat space cosmology, the total energy density is zero. The gravitational energy density is negative and cancels the matter energy density. The RTG black hole solution has metric components that decay but do not change sign. Time keeps its usual role in the interior of the RTG black hole. The transition layer width is approximately 10^-9 times the Planck length for solar mass. The theory makes sense only for masses greater than 10^3 solar masses. The time for an outside observer to see matter hit the center is finite. The cosmological model coincides with the ΛCDM model at large times. The model predicts an initial inflation scenario starting at t = −∞. The vacuum energy vanishes because the cosmological constant cancels the bimetric terms.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The field theoretic approach is equivalent to the curved space description in standard GTR. The bimetric theory forces a separate description of the Minkowski metric. Gravitation is viewed most naturally as a field in flat space in the RTG. The quantum version of RTG involves quantization of fields, not space. Clusters of galaxies do not move away; the speed of light changes with time. The separation of curved space into flat space and field has implications for quantum gravity.

Contradictions And Limitations
The theory has self-repulsive properties for matter falling onto a black hole in the negative Λ case. The Logunov version with negative ρbi does not allow a proper black hole solution. The approach makes sense only for masses greater than 10^3 solar masses. The Schwarzschild black hole cannot obey energy-momentum conservation if the central mass is smeared. The paper notes that changes to GTR have mostly met deep troubles.

Claims
Gravitation can be consistently described as a field in flat Minkowski space with a proper energy-momentum tensor. The gravitational energy-momentum tensor is derived from the Einstein equations. The tensor is conserved in Minkowski space. Standard GTR only has a quasi energy-momentum tensor. This allows for a clear accounting of energy transfer in gravitational waves.
The Relativistic Theory of Gravitation (RTG) with a positive cosmological constant resolves the black hole singularity. The metric components remain positive in the interior. Escape is, in principle, possible. The solution is only valid for masses above a certain threshold. This provides a singularity-free alternative to the standard Schwarzschild black hole.
The total energy of the universe is zero in this framework. Gravitational energy cancels material energy in flat cosmology. Vacuum energy vanishes due to bimetric cancellation.  This supports the idea that the universe has no net energy.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
The paper compares the RTG solution to the standard Schwarzschild solution. The effect of the bimetric term is analyzed for different mass scales. The paper discusses the limitations of the Logunov version with negative ρbi.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 shows the black hole functions U(r), V(r), and W(r) for the RTG solution. The figure compares the RTG solution to the Schwarzschild solution. It illustrates that U and V decay rapidly inside the horizon.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is a singularity-free black hole solution in a bimetric theory of gravitation. 2. The strongest evidence is the analytical derivation showing total energy cancellation in cosmology. 3. The future path involves studying realistic equations of state and quantum aspects of RTG.
